title: Hot-standby weight residency and KV hydration strategy for cold-start mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated pools occasionally suffer multi-second cold starts when model weights are not resident and KV cache is empty, causing request latency spikes that violate throughput SLAs. This ticket proposes a hot-standby residency model for weight placement combined with a staged KV hydration pipeline to reduce tail latency while keeping memory and startup costs predictable.

Goals:
- Ensure bounded cold-start latency (95th and 99th) for provisioned instances under committed throughput guarantees.
- Minimize additional memory/GPU-residency overhead across fleet.
- Integrate with autoscaler so that scale-outs maintain the same residency guarantees without excessive cost.

Approach overview:
1) Weight residency tiers: maintain a small hot-standby set of warm replicas that keep full model weights resident (resident-set) per shard. Use an LRU-ish residency score that favors recent / high-traffic model variants and customer pinning.
2) Streaming-weight attach: when a new worker is provisioned, stream critical layers (first/last N blocks and attention weights) to achieve partial functionality within SLO and continue background stream of remaining weights.
3) KV hydration pipeline: hydrate KV cache deterministically for common prefixes using sampled request traces and model-aware prefix expansion (top-100 prefixes per endpoint). Hydration happens in three phases: immediate on-attach (top prefixes), background batch-fill (long tail prefixes), and on-request lazy fill.
4) Fleet controls & admission: tie autoscaler admission to residency budget. New node creation checks a residency budget token; if budget exhausted, scale requests either queue briefly or fallback to smaller-compatible model variant.
5) Eviction & residency maintenance: use memory-aware eviction that considers model load time and recent QPS; evict coldest large models first, keep small/latency-sensitive models resident.
6) Telemetry & feedback loop: add residency metrics (resident_ratio, attach_time_p50/p95, kv_hydration_latency) and a regression alerting rule.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full preloading increases cost (more memory/GPU) but minimizes latency. We pick a hybrid streaming model to balance cost vs. tail latency.
- Deterministic prefix hydration reduces request variance but needs accurate prefix sampling; we will iterate sampling windows.
- Admission controls add complexity to the autoscaler but keep SLAs predictable under sudden spikes.

Rollout plan:
- Spike and prototype in a canary pool with 5% of Dedicated capacity (safety window).
- Run chaos tests (node cold restart, eviction storms) and compare attach_time and request P95 against baseline.
- Add runtime flag to toggle resident-set sizing and prefix count per endpoint.
- Gradual ramp to 50% then full after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Telemetry & success criteria:
- 95th latency for provisioned endpoints reduced by >=50% on canary compared to baseline.
- Attach_time_p95 <= 1.2s for most models under the hot-standby strategy.
- KV hit rate improvement of +20% within first 30s of attach for hydrated endpoints.

Backward compatibility:
- Default behavior remains unchanged for non-dedicated or unpinned models.
- Customers can opt out of residency via API flag or keep pinned models which will always be resident.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype hot-standby resident set implemented and configurable via runtime flags
Streaming-weight attach reduces initial attach latency vs full load measured in canary cluster
KV hydration pipeline increases initial KV hit rate by at least 20% in 30s for targeted endpoints
Autoscaler respects residency budget tokens and exposes admission metrics
Dashboard tiles for resident_ratio, attach_time_p50/p95, kv_hydration_latency created
Documentation and migration guide for Dedicated customers published
